findings.explanation: render_object_edit and render_object_preview (cms/views.py:365-370) delegate to render_object_endpoint, which for PageContent fetches the object with `model.admin_manager...get(pk=object_id)` (cms/views.py:305) and renders the full toolbar/content (cms/views.py:350-362) without ever calling user_can_view_page. A view-restricted page is therefore rendered to an authenticated staff user who has no view permission. This PR itself exposes the issue: it adds a view-permission guard only to render_object_structure (cms/views.py:259-260) and adds tests that assert the edit/preview endpoints should return 404 for a non-permitted staff user (cms/tests/test_views.py:571-584), confirming the edit/preview path has no such authorization check.

Typically, you will want it to copy related objects. To do this you should create a
method called ``copy_relations`` on your plugin model, that receives the **old
instance** of the plugin as an argument.

You may however decide that the related objects shouldn't be copied - you may want to
leave them alone, for example. Or, you might even want to choose some altogether
different relations for it, or to create new ones when it's copied... it depends on your
plugin and the way you want it to work.

If you do want to copy related objects, you'll need to do this in two slightly different
ways, depending on whether your plugin has relations *to* or *from* other objects that
need to be copied too:

For foreign key relations *from* other objects
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

Your plugin may have items with foreign keys to it, which will typically be the case if
you set it up so that they are inlines in its admin. So you might have two models, one
for the plugin and one for those items:

.. code-block::

    class ArticlePluginModel(CMSPlugin):

Both global page permissions and per-page permissions can be assigned to users or groups of users.

*Menu visibility* determines who'll be able to see the page in navigation menus - everyone, or logged in or anonymous users

published. Adding a view restriction will allow you to set this. Note that this doesn't apply any
